meta.title: Curated disease information for the TerraByte disease model classes
rules: Text is written in our own words. The cited NIPHM/DPPQS package is the crop-level reference; cultural measures are standard IPM practice and still need review by an agronomist (reviewed_by_agronomist: false).

Chemical options are listed only where the cited NIPHM/DPPQS AESA-based IPM package names them for that crop and disease; banned or restricted active ingredients are never listed (see banned_active_ingredients).
Chemical options are shown only for confident results.
meta.chemical_disclaimer: Guidance only. The IPM packages date from 2014-2017: check that the product has a current CIB&RC label claim for this crop, read the label, wear protective equipment, observe the waiting period before harvest, and consult your KVK or agriculture officer.
meta.no_chemical_text: No chemical option is listed here. Consult your agriculture officer or KVK before using any pesticide.

capsicum__bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease spread by infected seed and rain splash.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown
Leaf drop; scabby spots on fruit
cultural: Use disease-free seed and seedlings.
Avoid overhead irrigation; remove crop debris.
Rotate with non-solanaceous crops.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Chilli

capsicum__healthy.description: No disease symptoms were recognised on this leaf.
cultural: Keep scouting the field weekly; check several plants, not just one leaf.
Remove weeds and volunteer plants that can carry pests and diseases.

cultural: Use disease-free seed and seedlings; avoid overhead irrigation; rotate crops.

chilli__cercospora_leaf_spot.description: A fungal leaf spot favoured by humid weather.
symptoms: Round spots with light grey centres and dark borders (frog-eye)
cultural: Remove infected leaves and crop debris; avoid overhead irrigation; rotate crops.

chilli__leaf_curl_virus.description: A virus disease spread by whitefly; infected plants cannot be cured.
symptoms: Upward curling and puckering of leaves
Small leaves, stunted plants, few fruits
cultural: Raise seedlings under insect-proof net; use healthy seedlings.
Rogue out infected plants; use yellow sticky traps to monitor whitefly.

chilli__nutrient_deficiency.description: Leaf colour changes caused by a lack of one or more nutrients, not by a disease.
symptoms: Yellowing or discoloration of leaves without spots
cultural: Get a soil test and apply fertiliser according to it.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Chilli

chilli__white_spot.description: White spots on leaves as labelled in the source dataset; the cause is not specified.
symptoms: White or pale spots on leaves
cultural: Ask an expert to identify the cause before treating.

cotton__alternaria_leaf_spot.description: A fungal leaf spot common on stressed or older leaves.
symptoms: Brown circular spots with concentric rings; leaves drop
cultural: Give balanced nutrition (avoid potassium deficiency); remove infected debris.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Cotton

cotton__bacterial_blight.description: A bacterial disease spread by infected seed and rain splash.
symptoms: Angular water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown
Black lesions on veins and stems
cultural: Use acid-delinted or treated, disease-free seed.
Remove and destroy infected plant debris; rotate crops.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Cotton

cotton__fusarium_wilt.description: A soil-borne wilt; affected plants cannot recover.
symptoms: Yellowing and wilting of leaves, starting from the lower ones
Brown discoloration inside the stem
cultural: Grow tolerant varieties; rotate with non-host crops.
Uproot and destroy wilted plants; apply organic manure.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Cotton

cotton__healthy.description: No disease symptoms were recognised on this leaf.

cotton__verticillium_wilt.description: A soil-borne wilt favoured by cool weather.
symptoms: Yellow patches between veins, leaf drying and wilting
cultural: Rotate with non-host crops such as cereals; remove infected plants.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Cotton

grape__bacterial_leaf_spot.description: A bacterial disease that spreads in warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Small dark angular spots on leaves, often along veins
cultural: Collect and destroy infected plant parts.
Increase air movement in the vineyard.
Remove diseased canes during pruning.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Grapes

grape__black_rot.description: A fungal disease (rare in India) that affects leaves and berries.
symptoms: Brown circular leaf spots with dark borders and black dots
Berries shrivel and turn black
cultural: Remove mummified berries and infected canes; keep the canopy open.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Grapes

grape__downy_mildew.description: A major grape disease in humid or rainy weather (common after rain in Nashik).
symptoms: Yellow oily spots on the upper leaf surface
White downy growth on the underside of leaves
Affected bunches shrivel
cultural: Prune after the second week of October; remove and destroy affected parts at pruning.
Collect infected leaves and dispose of them in a compost pit.

chemical.dose: 1 kg in 300–400 l of water per acre

grape__esca.description: A trunk disease complex; leaf symptoms appear in summer.
symptoms: Tiger-stripe pattern: yellow or red areas between veins that dry out
cultural: Prune in dry weather and remove dead wood; protect large pruning wounds.

grape__leaf_blight.description: A fungal leaf spot that appears late in the season.
symptoms: Dark brown irregular spots on leaves; leaves dry and drop early
cultural: Remove fallen leaves; keep the canopy open.

grape__powdery_mildew.description: A fungal disease favoured by dry, cloudy weather and dense canopies.
symptoms: White to grey powdery growth on leaves, shoots and berries
Berries crack
cultural: Manage the canopy for air movement and light; reduce humidity in the vineyard.
Use under-vine irrigation and avoid excess water.

chemical.dose: 0.75–1 kg in 300–400 l of water per acre

maize__common_rust.description: A fungal disease that forms rust-coloured pustules on leaves.
symptoms: Small, raised, reddish-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces
cultural: Grow resistant or tolerant hybrids.
Remove volunteer plants and weeds.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Maize

maize__gray_leaf_spot.description: A fungal leaf disease favoured by warm, humid weather and crop residue.
symptoms: Long, narrow, rectangular grey-brown lesions between leaf veins
cultural: Rotate crops and manage infected residue.
Grow tolerant hybrids.

symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions on leaves
cultural: Grow resistant hybrids.
Rotate crops and manage infected residue.

pigeonpea__leaf_spot.description: A fungal leaf spot favoured by humid weather.
symptoms: Small brown spots on leaves; leaves may drop
cultural: Remove infected leaves and crop debris; rotate crops.

pigeonpea__leaf_webber.description: Caterpillars web leaves and flowers together and feed inside.
symptoms: Leaves and flowers webbed together; feeding damage inside the webs
cultural: Hand-pick and destroy webbed leaves with larvae; conserve natural enemies.

pigeonpea__sterility_mosaic.description: A virus disease spread by eriophyid mites; affected plants bear few or no pods.
symptoms: Light green mosaic on small leaves
Bushy plants without flowers or pods
cultural: Grow resistant varieties; uproot and destroy infected plants early.
Remove volunteer and ratoon pigeonpea plants that carry the mites.

symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves
Yellowing and drying of leaves
cultural: Use healthy seed tubers and varieties with resistance where available.
Remove crop debris; give balanced fertiliser.

chemical.dose: 600–800 g in 300 l of water per acre

potato__late_blight.description: The most destructive potato disease; spreads fast in cool, humid weather.
symptoms: Water-soaked, dark patches on leaf tips and edges
White mould under leaves
Brown rot in tubers
cultural: Use healthy seed tubers and resistant varieties (several Kufri varieties are resistant).
Use short-duration varieties; destroy infected haulms and cull piles.

rice__bacterial_blight.description: A bacterial disease favoured by high nitrogen and flooding.
symptoms: Yellow to white stripes starting from leaf tips and edges
Leaves dry and turn straw-coloured
cultural: Grow resistant varieties; avoid excess nitrogen.
Do not let water flow from infected to healthy fields; keep bunds clean.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Rice

rice__blast.description: A fungal disease of leaves, nodes and panicles.
symptoms: Spindle-shaped spots with grey centres and brown edges on leaves
Neck of the panicle turns black and breaks
cultural: Grow resistant varieties; avoid excess nitrogen; remove weed hosts.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Rice

rice__brown_spot.description: A fungal disease common in nutrient-poor or stressed crops.
symptoms: Oval brown spots with grey centres on leaves
cultural: Use healthy seed; correct soil nutrient deficiencies (balanced fertiliser).

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Rice

rice__tungro.description: A virus disease spread by green leafhoppers.
symptoms: Yellow to orange leaves starting from the tip
Stunted plants with fewer tillers
cultural: Grow resistant varieties; remove infected plants and stubble; synchronise planting.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Rice

soybean__bacterial_blight.description: A bacterial disease spread by seed and rain splash in cool, wet weather.
symptoms: Small angular water-soaked spots that turn brown with a yellow halo
cultural: Use clean seed; rotate crops and bury or remove residue.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Soyabean

soybean__cercospora_leaf_blight.description: A fungal disease of upper leaves late in the season.
symptoms: Purple-bronze, leathery discoloration of upper leaves
Purple staining of seeds
cultural: Use healthy seed; rotate crops and manage residue.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Soyabean

soybean__healthy.description: No disease symptoms were recognised on this leaf.
cultural: Keep scouting the field weekly; check several plants, not just one leaf.
Remove weeds and volunteer plants that can carry pests and diseases.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Soyabean

soybean__rust.description: A fungal disease that can cause early leaf drop in humid weather.
symptoms: Small tan to reddish-brown lesions with pustules, mostly on the underside of leaves
Leaves yellow and drop early
cultural: Sow at the recommended time and grow tolerant varieties.
Avoid very dense sowing; remove volunteer soybean plants.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Soyabean

soybean__sudden_death_syndrome.description: A soil-borne root disease whose leaf symptoms appear around flowering.
symptoms: Yellow patches between veins that turn brown while veins stay green
Leaves drop
cultural: Improve drainage; rotate crops; avoid soil compaction.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Soyabean

sugarcane__healthy.description: No disease symptoms were recognised on this leaf.
cultural: Keep scouting the field weekly; check several plants, not just one leaf.
Remove weeds and volunteer plants that can carry pests and diseases.

sugarcane__mosaic.pathogen: Sugarcane mosaic virus (aphid-borne, and through infected setts)
sugarcane__mosaic.description: A virus disease; infected setts carry it to the next crop.
symptoms: Pale green and dark green streaks or mottling on leaves
cultural: Use healthy setts from disease-free seed nurseries; rogue out infected clumps.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Sugarcane

sugarcane__red_rot.description: A serious sugarcane disease spread mainly through infected setts.
symptoms: Drying of leaves from the top
Red inner tissue with white patches when the cane is split
Sour smell
cultural: Plant healthy setts from disease-free nurseries; grow resistant varieties.
Uproot and destroy affected clumps; avoid ratooning a diseased crop; rotate crops.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Sugarcane

sugarcane__rust.description: A fungal leaf disease favoured by humid weather.
symptoms: Small yellow spots that become orange-brown pustules on leaves
cultural: Grow resistant varieties; avoid excess nitrogen.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Sugarcane

sugarcane__yellow_leaf.description: A virus disease that causes yellowing of the leaf midrib.
symptoms: Yellowing of the midrib on the underside of leaves, spreading to the leaf blade
cultural: Use healthy setts (e.g. from tissue-culture or heat-treated seed nurseries).

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Sugarcane

tomato__bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease spread by rain splash, infected seed and transplants.
symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves, sometimes with a yellow halo
Raised scabby spots on fruit
cultural: Use seed and seedlings from disease-free nurseries.
Avoid overhead irrigation and working in the field when plants are wet.
Remove crop debris after harvest and rotate with non-solanaceous crops.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Tomato

tomato__early_blight.description: A fungal leaf disease that starts on older, lower leaves and spreads upwards.
symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (target-like) on older leaves
Yellowing around the spots; leaves dry and drop
cultural: Use resistant or tolerant varieties.
Change the nursery bed location every season; remove weeds and volunteer tomato plants.
Avoid planting overlapping tomato crops in adjacent fields; fertilise properly.

chemical.dose: 400 g in 200 l of water per acre

tomato__late_blight.description: A fast-spreading disease in cool, humid or rainy weather that can destroy a crop in days.
symptoms: Large, water-soaked, grey-green to brown patches on leaves
White mould on the underside of leaves in humid weather
Brown, firm patches on fruit
cultural: Keep the field clean (field sanitation) and destroy alternate hosts.
Give light irrigation; avoid long leaf wetness.
Remove and destroy badly affected plants.

chemical.dose: 600 g in 200–300 l of water per acre

tomato__leaf_mold.description: A fungal disease mostly of humid, poorly ventilated crops (e.g. polyhouses).
symptoms: Pale yellow patches on the upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown velvety mould on the underside
cultural: Improve air movement: wider spacing, staking and pruning lower leaves.
Reduce humidity in protected cultivation; avoid wetting the leaves.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Tomato

tomato__mosaic_virus.description: A virus disease spread by contact (hands, tools) and infected seed. It cannot be cured.
symptoms: Light and dark green mottling of leaves
Distorted, fern-like leaves; stunted plants
cultural: Remove and destroy infected plants; wash hands and tools after handling them.
Use healthy seed and seedlings.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Tomato

tomato__septoria_leaf_spot.description: A fungal leaf spot that starts on lower leaves after wet weather.
symptoms: Many small round spots with dark borders and grey centres
Tiny black dots in the centre of the spots; heavy leaf drop
cultural: Remove and destroy infected lower leaves and crop debris.
Rotate with non-solanaceous crops and avoid overhead irrigation.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Tomato

tomato__spider_mites.description: Tiny mites that suck sap from the underside of leaves, mostly in hot, dry weather.
symptoms: Fine yellow speckles on leaves; leaves turn bronze and dry
Fine webbing on the underside of leaves
cultural: Conserve natural enemies such as predatory mites; avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum sprays.
Keep plants well watered and remove heavily infested leaves.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Tomato

tomato__target_spot.description: A fungal leaf spot favoured by warm, humid weather.
symptoms: Brown spots with light centres and rings on leaves, stems and fruit
cultural: Improve air movement and avoid long leaf wetness.
Remove crop debris and rotate crops.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Tomato

tomato__yellow_leaf_curl_virus.description: A virus disease spread by whitefly. Infected plants cannot be cured.
symptoms: Upward or downward curling and crinkling of leaves
Yellow leaf edges, stunted plants
Few flowers and fruits
cultural: Raise the nursery under insect-proof net to keep whitefly out.
Remove and destroy infected seedlings and plants (roguing); use healthy seedlings only.
Grow barrier crops such as maize or sorghum around the field; use yellow sticky traps (about 10 per acre) to monitor whitefly.

sources.title: NIPHM / DPPQS: AESA based IPM package – Tomato
